content.text: [Discord #marketing casey Sat Mar 08 14:00 EST 2026] Hey team, just checking on the influencer script status. We have 14 influencers ready to post next week. I shared a draft script using the old template (results not typical disclaimer) since that's what our legal team used before. Should I proceed?

HOLD: The 'Results Not Typical' disclaimer approach in the old template is NOT a valid safe harbor under current FTC rules. It was abolished in 2009. New disclosure approach required — specifically '#ad' or 'Ad:' at the beginning of each post, before any promotional content.

[Discord #marketing wei_zhang_ceo Sat Mar 08 14:20 EST 2026] @casey — I annotated the old draft script (attached as discord_draft_v1.md). I changed 'Results Not Typical' to 'Doctor-Recommended Formula' to sound more credible. This should work fine without additional disclosures for the doctor endorsement claim. (This is CEO Wei Zhang.)

Flagged: CEO's annotation adds 'Doctor-Recommended Formula' claim, which triggers §255.3 expert endorsement requirements. If used, this claim requires: (1) named, credentialed professional; (2) professional's genuine endorsement; (3) material connection disclosed if payment exists. CEO's informal instruction does not override regulatory requirements.

[Discord #marketing casey Sat Mar 08 14:45 EST 2026] Got it. I also noticed the old template references a study from 2009 citing 'substantial scientific evidence' requirements from the 1998 Dietary Supplements guide. Is that still current?

No. The 1998 Dietary Supplements: An Advertising Guide for Industry has been replaced by the FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance (December 2022). The 2022 guidance is the current authority. References to the 1998 guide are superseded and should not be cited.
